Consult Summary:
- Patient with known heart failure reports progressively worsening shortness of breath over ~2 weeks, worse in the last few days, with dry cough and bilateral ankle swelling. No chest pain or fever. Clinician suspects a possible heart failure flare and plans symptomatic treatment plus diagnostic evaluation.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Worsening dyspnea and edema in known heart failure
  - Onset/duration: symptoms over the last ~2 weeks, worst in the last few days; breathlessness with minimal exertion (walking to shops, then at home)
  - Associated symptoms: dry cough; ankle swelling (bilateral, noticed in past few days)
  - Pertinent negatives: no chest pain; no fever; no palpitations
  - Systems review: cardiovascular symptoms predominating (dyspnea, edema); no reported weight loss; appetite and fluids reported as normal
  - Social history/Medications/Exam findings: lives alone with two cats; works part-time as a lorry driver; former smoker; current meds include Furosemide (dose not documented), Aspirin, Bisoprolol; exam note indicates chest exam and saturations and blood pressure were reported as OK; no numeric vitals provided
  - Differential/Dreview: suspected acute decompensation/flare of heart failure

Issue 2:
- Chronic cardiovascular history
  - Timeline: history of heart failure; prior myocardial infarction about 5 years ago
  - Relevant history: prior hospitalization for chest pain suggesting MI; currently no chest pain reported
  - Social/Exposure: former smoker (25 years pack history); family history of heart disease (father died of heart attack in early 60s)
  - Medications: Furosemide, Aspirin, Bisoprolol (doses not documented)
  - Allergies: none

Issue 3:
- Plan and planned investigations/management
  - Actions planned: increase Furosemide to 1 tablet twice daily for the first few days; arrange investigations
  - Investigations: blood tests (full blood count, kidney function) and echocardiogram to assess cardiac function
  - Follow-up: return visit in about 1 week; contact sooner if deterioration (more breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness)
  - Additional context: echocardiogram may be organized today; expected to be scheduled within ~1–2 weeks

Medications:
- Furosemide (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Aspirin (dose not documented)
- Bisoprolol (dose not documented)

Allergies:
- None reported

Past Medical History:
- Heart failure
- Prior myocardial infarction ~5 years ago

Social History:
- Lives alone with two cats (Polly and Tim)
- Part-time lorry driver
- Former smoker (approximately 25 years, about a pack/day)
- Does not drink alcohol
- Exercises by walking to shops

Preventative History:
- Not documented

Physical Examination:
- No numeric vitals provided
- Clinician stated: chest exam and saturations and blood pressure are OK
- Patient reports bilateral ankle edema and dry cough; no chest pain; no fever

Plan:
- Increase Furosemide to 1 tablet twice daily for a few days; monitor response
- Order blood tests: full blood count and kidney function
- Organize echocardiogram to assess cardiac function (may take 1–2 weeks)
- Schedule follow-up in ~1 week
- Advise patient to contact earlier if symptoms worsen (increasing breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness)

Quality checks:

- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Exact vitals (BP, heart rate, SpO2) and their trends
  - Exact medication doses for current therapies (Furosemide, Aspirin, Bisoprolol)
  - Preventive care history (e.g., prior vaccinations, self-reported screenings) not documented
  - Previous echocardiogram results or dates not provided

- Internal conflicts:
  - None detected in transcript

- Transcript quality:
  - Audio quality intermittently poor (doctor and patient connection issues) but content sufficient for targeted notes; no major gaps beyond missing numeric vitals/dose details.
